themes.title: AI Everything Abu Dhabi: the Gulf's AI showpiece opens
themes.summary: Abu Dhabi's AI Everything summit opened with more than 400 AI companies, 20 unicorns and 200 investors managing $100 billion, focused on moving AI from pilots to large-scale deployment. The UAE is using the event to press its workforce and state-capability agenda, reporting 80,000 government workers trained as AI super users and a state AI council reviewing progress.
themes.angle: The GCC's flagship argument that governments, not just labs, can drive AI adoption at scale.

themes.title: Open-weight comeback: Reflection Beam and Mistral vs China
themes.summary: Reflection AI released its first open-source model, Beam, joining Mistral in a push Axios frames as a Western open-weight comeback against China's recent lead. The models give businesses and governments alternatives to the closed ecosystems of the largest US labs.
themes.angle: Procurement is becoming a real strategic choice: open weights are now credible third options.

themes.title: SpaceX eyes $40B Nvidia chip war chest
themes.summary: SpaceX is in talks to raise $40 billion in debt, in financing led by Apollo, to buy Nvidia chips — the latest sign of vast spending on AI infrastructure. Executives tie compute and energy as the two binding constraints of the AI boom.
themes.angle: AI capex just moved onto the credit markets; watch for leverage to become the system-level risk.

themes.title: OpenAI: math results plus an enterprise agent push
themes.summary: OpenAI published new results on open math problems from an internal frontier model and shared Lean proof formalizations on GitHub; The Information reports over 700 papers with AI-made solutions. The lab also showcased longer-running agent workflows with enterprise partners Atlassian, Ironclad and Jump Trading.
themes.angle: Science credibility plus enterprise agents: OpenAI is selling both frontier and deployment.

themes.title: AI-enabled cyber risk: South Korea probes AI hacks
themes.summary: South Korea is investigating whether AI was used in hacking its banks, with President Lee Jae Myung warning of a 'completely new kind of crisis'. Axios separately reports AI tools are flooding into underground cybercrime markets, making hacking capabilities cheaper to buy.
themes.angle: The first major state-level probe of AI-in-the-attack is a preview of board-level cyber risk.

themes.title: GCC AI capital: Korea-Saudi ties, National Vault, Inception42
themes.summary: Korea and Saudi Arabia are widening cooperation beyond energy into AI, data centres and aerospace. The UAE advanced its National Vault cyber-resilience plans with Dell, CPX and the Cyber Security Council, while ADGM's Inception42 launched an AI product aimed at executive decision-making.
themes.angle: Gulf AI is moving from grand pledges to deal-making and deployed state capability.

themes.title: Washington's Super Intelligence machine
themes.summary: President Trump's new 'Super Intelligence' task force is working to reconcile divided cabinet factions into a coherent AI policy. The Justice Department has told staff to use the term 'super intelligence' under the executive order, and regulators and watchers debate what it means.
themes.angle: Language is policy: renaming AI changes how the federal bureaucracy and markets frame risk.

themes.title: Frontier releases: EmbeddingGemma 2 goes open

themes.angle: Small open models keep shifting the inference-cost curve, including for on-device use.
